subject: Can I mix categorical and continuous variables in SEM ?

messages.author: 4a0d6ff9ce3b1d6b
messages.subject: Can I mix categorical and continuous variables in SEM ?
parts:
Dear lavaan community,

I'm trying to analyze panel data with lavaan (cross-lagged effect model).
But there's some missing questions in specific wave.

For example,
I wish I could use latent variable f1 estimated by question A and B, and latent f2 estimated by question C and D.
But some waves don't have question D.

In this case, can I use question C alone instead of using latent variable f2 (estimated by C&D)?

I think the sole question (C in the former case) can be treated as continuous theoretically.

And if I can, is the lavaan code: lavaan(model, data, ordered = D)  OK?

Any advice will help me!
Ashu

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Can I mix categorical and continuous variables in SEM ?
parts:
Can I mix categorical and continuous variables in SEM?

Yes.
can I use question C alone instead of using latent variable f2 (estimated by C&D)?

Yes, you can treat f2 as a single-indicator construct (i.e., leave D out of your model), but do that at all time points if you want to interpret your autoregressive paths or compare cross-lagged parameters over time.  Make sure f1 has loading-invariance constraints in place over time as well (although it is not really testable with so few indicators).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
